# Pin tumbler

From Lockwiki

[Jump to navigation](#column-one)[Jump to search](#searchInput)

Pin tumbler

---

[![](/images/thumb/3/31/Lockwiki_Medeco_pins.jpg/300px-Lockwiki_Medeco_pins.jpg)](/index.php/File:Lockwiki_Medeco_pins.jpg)

[Medeco](/index.php/Medeco "Medeco") biaxial key, pin pairs, springs, and chamber caps.

A **pin-tumbler** is a [cylinder](/index.php/Cylinder "Cylinder") based [lock](/index.php/Lock "Lock") design that uses movable pins to prevent rotation of the [plug](/index.php/Plug "Plug"). A [key](/index.php/Key "Key") is used to properly elevate pins to allow the plug to rotate and the locking [bolt](/index.php/Bolt "Bolt") to be retracted.

The pin-tumbler is currently one of the most widely used lock designs in the world. Minor changes to the positions of pin-tumbler components are the basis for [dimple](/index.php/Dimple "Dimple") and axial/tubular lock designs.

## History

Pin-tumbler locks were originally invented in ancient Egypt. The design used a series of single pins that, when locked, would prevent movement of a bolt by resting inside the bolt itself. The key was used to raise pins out of the bolt, allowing it to retract. This was the first use of a [shear line](/index.php/Shear_line "Shear line"), a major discovery that is the basis for all cylinder based locks in modern use. Early pin tumbler locks, bolts, and keys were all made with wood, but eventually brass and iron were used. Many cultures adopted the design throughout history, but it would not be widely used until [Linus Yale Sr.](/index.php/Linus_Yale_Sr "Linus Yale Sr") and [Linus Yale, Jr.](/index.php/Linus_Yale_Jr "Linus Yale Jr") modified the pin-tumbler design in the mid 1800s.

Linus Yale Sr. improved the Egyptian design with the idea of pin pairs. In the original lock pins were required to be raised high enough to clear the bolt, but were not checked to make sure they weren't raised higher than necessary. The addition of a second pin in each chamber allowed for [positive locking](/index.php?title=Positive_locking&action=edit&redlink=1 "Positive locking (page does not exist)") when components were raised too high. In this design, the key had to properly raise the pin pairs so that they could separate at the shear line, allowing the locking bolt to be retracted. Yale Sr. also added springs above the pin pairs to force them down to their locked position when no key is inserted.

Linus Yale Jr. continued his father's work by improving the design of the pin-tumbler. He made it smaller, more reliable, and changed the design of the key to be flat instead of fluted. This type of key is still used by modern pin-tumbler locks.

The design of the pin-tumbler lock has remained virtually unchanged since the Yale family's contributions. [Master keying](/index.php/Master_Key "Master Key") allows the addition of pins in each chamber to provide various methods of keying a particular lock or group of locks. Other improvements have been in the form of auxiliary security mechanisms to prevent compromise. [Security pins](/index.php/Security_pin "Security pin"), [sidebars](/index.php/Sidebar "Sidebar"), and [side pins](/index.php/Side_pin "Side pin") were created to frustrate [lockpicking](/index.php/Lockpicking "Lockpicking"). Other anti-picking modifications exist, such as [rotation](/index.php/Axial_rotation "Axial rotation") or [telescoping](/index.php/Telescoping_pin "Telescoping pin"). Finally, ball bearings and hardened steel rods or discs are now inserted into the plug or cylinder to protect the pin stacks against [destructive entry](/index.php/Destructive_Entry "Destructive Entry").

## Principles of operation

Pin tumblers are a series of pin stacks pushed to a default position by a spring. The default position of each pin stack causes the driver pin (the one in contact with the spring) to block rotation of the plug. Each pin stack must be properly aligned to allow pins to separate at the [shear line](/index.php/Shear_line "Shear line"). Once all pin stacks are properly aligned the plug can freely rotate and [actuate](/index.php/Actuator "Actuator") the locking bolt to lock or unlock the lock.

An incorrect key will not align all components correctly; rotation of the plug will be blocked at the shear-line.

* [![](/images/thumb/6/68/Pin_tumbler_no_key.jpg/120px-Pin_tumbler_no_key.jpg)](/index.php/File:Pin_tumbler_no_key.jpg)

  A pin-tumbler cylinder, no key inserted.
* [![](/images/thumb/e/ec/Pin_tumbler_with_key.jpg/120px-Pin_tumbler_with_key.jpg)](/index.php/File:Pin_tumbler_with_key.jpg)

  A pin-tumbler cylinder, correct key inserted.
* [![](/images/thumb/1/15/Pin_tumbler_unlocked.jpg/120px-Pin_tumbler_unlocked.jpg)](/index.php/File:Pin_tumbler_unlocked.jpg)

  A pin-tumbler cylinder, correct key inserted and [plug](/index.php/Plug "Plug") rotated.
* [![](/images/thumb/c/cf/Pin_tumbler_bad_key.jpg/120px-Pin_tumbler_bad_key.jpg)](/index.php/File:Pin_tumbler_bad_key.jpg)

  A pin-tumbler cylinder, incorrect key inserted.

## Components

Key pins (bottom pins)
:   The pins that are touched by the key. Key pins are sized differently corresponding to the different depth cuts on the key. When the correct key is inserted, all key pins are aligned at the [shear line](/index.php/Shear_line "Shear line"), allowing the plug to rotate.

Driver pins (top pins)
:   The pins placed between the key pins and the spings. In their resting position, the driver pins block rotation of the plug. In more advanced pin-tumblers, driver pins may be sized inverse to the key pins to defend against [decoding](/index.php/Decoding "Decoding") and attacks via [comb picks](/index.php/Comb_pick "Comb pick").

Springs
:   Springs placed above the pin stacks push pins down to the their resting position, ensuring that pins cannot be trapped above the [shear line](/index.php/Shear_line "Shear line") while the plug is in the default position.

Plug
:   The [plug](/index.php/Plug "Plug") is the inner piece of the lock that rotates upon insertion and tension of the correct key. The plug is connected to the cam to actuate the bolt mechanism when rotated.

Cylinder
:   The [cylinder](/index.php/Cylinder "Cylinder") is the outer piece of the lock that houses the upper pin chambers and the plug. Driver pins and springs are trapped in the cylinder's pin chambers, commonly referred to as the **bible**, when the correct key is used and plug rotated.

Cam
:   The [cam](/index.php/Cam "Cam") is an extension connected to the back of the plug which actuates the [bolt](/index.php/Bolt "Bolt") mechanism to lock or unlock the lock.

## Vulnerabilities

Pin-tumblers are vulnerable to a wide variety of attacks. The specifics of the pin-tumbler design and manufacturing tolerances will determine the exact vulnerabilities present, but most pin-tumblers are vulnerable to at least one or more of the following:

* [Lockpicking](/index.php/Lockpicking "Lockpicking")
* [Pick Guns](/index.php/Pick_Gun "Pick Gun")
* [Key Bumping](/index.php/Bumping "Bumping")
* [Tryout Keys](/index.php/Tryout_Keys "Tryout Keys")
* [Comb Picks](/index.php/Comb_Pick "Comb Pick")
* [Impressioning](/index.php/Impressioning "Impressioning")
* [Decoding](/index.php/Decoding "Decoding")
* [Bypass](/index.php/Bypass "Bypass")
* [Destructive Entry](/index.php/Destructive_Entry "Destructive Entry")
